spec.title: Merge ranges
spec.prompt:
Write solve(ranges) where ranges is a list of [start, end] pairs of
integers, each with start <= end, in any order.

Return the shortest list of [start, end] pairs, sorted by start, that covers
exactly the same numbers. Two ranges that share at least one number are one
range. A range covers BOTH of its endpoints: [1, 2] covers 1 and 2.

Ranges that merely touch across a gap, like [1, 2] and [4, 5], stay apart.
spec.ambiguity: Ends are inclusive, so [1,2] and [2,3] merge; [1,2] and [3,4] do not.

tests.name: shared endpoint
tests.why: both ranges cover the number 2

tests.name: disjoint
tests.why: a gap keeps them apart

tests.name: empty list
tests.why: nothing to merge

tests.name: nested
tests.why: a contained range disappears

tests.name: two points
tests.why: a point range covers one number, shared by both

tests.name: out of order
tests.why: the input order is not the answer's

tests.name: chain out of order
tests.why: merging can cascade once sorted

tests.name: adjacent integers
tests.why: 1..2 and 3..4 share no number

tests.name: gap merged
tests.why: betting that neighbouring integers merge

tests.name: ends exclusive
tests.why: betting the end is not covered

spec.title: Longest run
spec.prompt:
Write solve(xs) where xs is a list of integers.

Return the length of the longest run of equal elements in xs. A run is a
maximal block of neighbouring elements that are all equal to each other, so
[1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 1] has runs of length 2, 3 and 1 and the answer is 3.

A list with no elements has no runs at all.
spec.ambiguity: An empty list scores 0, and a run must be neighbouring: [1,2,1,2,1] is 1, not 3.

tests.name: empty list
tests.why: a list with no elements has no runs

tests.name: single element
tests.why: one element is a run of one

tests.name: leading pair
tests.why: the longest neighbouring block wins

tests.name: all distinct
tests.why: no two neighbours are equal

tests.name: one long run
tests.why: the whole list is one run

tests.name: alternating values
tests.why: equal elements that are not neighbours are not one run

tests.name: repeat after a gap
tests.why: the trailing 3 does not extend the leading run

tests.name: negatives
tests.why: negative values run like any other

tests.name: empty raises
tests.why: betting that an empty list is an error

tests.name: counts the value
tests.why: betting the run's value is returned, not its length

spec.title: Roman numerals
spec.prompt:
Write solve(n) where n is an integer.

Return the Roman numeral for n, written the way Romans wrote it on
monuments: the subtractive forms are used wherever they apply, so 4 is "IV",
9 is "IX", 40 is "XL", 90 is "XC", 400 is "CD" and 900 is "CM".

n is between 1 and 3999 inclusive; anything outside that range is not a
number this function can answer.
spec.ambiguity: Subtractive forms everywhere (400 is CD, 900 is CM); 0 and 4000 are errors, not numerals.

tests.name: three
tests.why: the plain additive case

tests.name: four
tests.why: the subtractive form for four

tests.name: nine
tests.why: the subtractive form for nine

tests.name: forty
tests.why: the subtractive form for forty

tests.name: forty four
tests.why: two subtractive forms in one numeral

tests.name: four hundred
tests.why: the subtractive form applies at the hundreds too

tests.name: nine hundred
tests.why: nine hundred is CM, never DCCCC

tests.name: mixed thousands
tests.why: CM and IV in the same numeral

tests.name: zero
tests.why: betting that zero answers the empty string

tests.name: over range
tests.why: betting that four thousand is just four Ms
